text:
Same structural issue as PKIX-fmtv.17 (just human-labeled in this session) and PKIX-fmtv.18 (same labeling, this session). The acceptance criterion is a per-purpose pass-rate baseline against pyca/cryptography's PolicyBuilder. PKITS chains uniformly fail through verify_* wrappers because PKITS EE certs lack any EKU and any SAN. pkix-difftest's existing corpora are chain-shape-only.

pyca's PolicyBuilder additionally enforces RFC 6125 hostname binding via DNSName(...) — that's its purpose-driving API. So pyca actively requires hostname-bearing leaves; PKITS leaves fail at PolicyBuilder construction time. No way around this without a curated SAN-bearing corpus.

Same two paths as .18:

(A) WAIT FOR CURATED CORPUS: blocked-on-deps until a corpus exists. AGENTS.md-aligned: pass-rate requires a corpus.

(B) RESCOPE DOWN: 8-fixture smoke test vs PolicyBuilder. Not a baseline.

Specific pyca finding worth recording: pyca's PolicyBuilder splits into build_server_verifier(DNSName) and build_client_verifier() with subtly different EKU semantics. The bead description doesn't address that S/MIME has no pyca verifier and code-signing has no pyca verifier — only TLS server / TLS client are testable against pyca. So even with a corpus, this bead's deliverable is necessarily TLS-only on the pyca side. That's not a problem (the bead acknowledges it) but it tightens the scope further: differential testing for non-TLS wrappers falls entirely to .18 (OpenSSL).

Recommend labeling human, waiting for the .17 decision. Releasing without claiming.
